feedback.problem: Given the function $f(x)=7-{x}^{7},$ which of the following statements are true?
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the stationary points. Differentiating $f(x)$ gives

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=-7{x}^{6}.
$$

Solving ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ gives

$$
-7{x}^{6}=0\,⟹\,x=0.
$$

So $x=0$ is the only stationary point of $f(x).$ Next, to determine whether this point is local maximum or minimum, we use the first derivative test.

Let's choose the test points $x=-1,1$ and evaluate the first derivative at these points.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(-1) & =-7(-1)^{6}=-7<0 \\ {f}^{′}(1) & =-7(1)^{6}=-7<0\end{aligned}
$$

We summarize the information in a table shown below.

| $x$ | $(-\infty ,0)$ | $0$ | $(0,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Test Point | $-1$ |  | $1$ |
| ${f}^{′}$ | $-$ | $0$ | $-$ |
| $f$ | $↘$ |  | $↘$ |

The first derivative does not change sign at $x=0.$ Therefore, we conclude that $x=0$ is neither a minimum nor a maximum.

Hence, the first derivative test shows that the function has no local extrema.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: The function $f(x)$ has no local extrema
